articles.title_en: Tree Cover Perforation and Malaria: Evidence from Colombia
articles.title_cn: 树冠穿孔与疟疾：来自哥伦比亚的证据
articles.abstract_en: A growing literature seeks to econometrically identify the link between tree cover change and malaria, two of the most pressing problems facing the Global South. However, we know little about the effect of tree cover fragmentation on malaria transmission, even though correlational evidence suggests that this effect may be important. We use municipality-level panel data from Colombia along with two-way fixed effects models to identify the effect on malaria incidence of changes in two measures of tree cover fragmentation—perforation and edge—as well as of a conventional measure of aggregate tree cover loss. We find that perforation in core areas of tree cover spurs malaria transmission. Evidence for the effects of changes in edge and aggregate loss is weaker. On average, a one-percentage-point increase in contemporaneous perforation leads to a 12.7% increase in malaria cases. This effect is stronger in municipalities with gold production and in those with coca production. These findings provide further evidence that forest conservation has significant benefits for local communities. They can also help stakeholders improve the efficacy of policies to stem malaria transmission.
articles.abstract_cn: 越来越多的文献试图通过计量经济学方法识别树冠变化与疟疾之间的联系，这是全球南方面临的两个最紧迫的问题。然而，尽管相关证据表明树冠破碎化对疟疾传播的影响可能很重要，但我们对树冠破碎化对疟疾传播的影响知之甚少。我们使用哥伦比亚市级面板数据以及双向固定效应模型，识别树冠破碎化的两个指标——穿孔和边缘——以及常规的总体树冠损失指标的变化对疟疾发病率的影响。我们发现，树冠核心区域的穿孔会促进疟疾传播。边缘变化和总体损失变化的证据较弱。平均而言，同期穿孔率每增加一个百分点，疟疾病例数就会增加12.7%。这种效应在金矿生产市和古柯生产市中更为显著。这些发现进一步证明，森林保护对当地社区具有显著益处。它们还可以帮助利益相关者提高遏制疟疾传播政策的有效性。

articles.title_en: Forest Cover and Dengue in Costa Rica: Panel Data Analysis of the Effects of Forest Cover Change on Hospital Admissions and Outbreaks
articles.title_cn: 哥斯达黎加的森林覆盖与登革热：森林覆盖变化对住院和疫情影响的面板数据分析
articles.abstract_en: Approximately 3.9 billion people are at risk of infection with dengue fever, a group of viruses transmitted by mosquitoes (Halstead in Annu Rev Entomol 53:273–291, 2008. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.ento.53.103106.0933262008 ; WHO in WHO | Dengue and severe dengue, Geneva, 2018). In 2019, Central America suffered a severe dengue epidemic (Salinas Maldonado in Un brote de dengue pone en alerta a Centroamérica | Sociedad | EL PAÍS, El País, 2019). Costa Rica witnessed an almost doubling of the number of dengue cases in the first 24 epidemiological weeks of 2019 compared to the same period in the previous year (Ávalos in Costa Rica casi duplica número de enfermos de dengue en lo que va del año, con respecto al 2018, La Nación, 2019). In the Americas, forest cover is thought to diminish anthropogenic habitats for mosquitoes while also increasing the presence of their predators (Vasilakis et al. in Nat Rev Microbiol 9:532–541, 2011. https://doi.org/10.1038/nrmicro2595 ; Weterings et al. in Basic Appl Ecol 15:486–495, 2014a. https://doi.org/10.1016/J.BAAE.2014.07.006 ). In this study, we estimate the marginal effects of increasing forest cover on dengue prevalence in Costa Rica using econometric models to relate hospital admission records to forest cover maps from 2001 and 2011. We find that increasing the percentage of forest cover significantly decreases both the number of hospital admissions for dengue and the probability of an outbreak. Using the same models, we predict that if forest cover had been increased by three percentage points during 10 years (0.29% per year), 29 dengue hospital admissions per year might have been avoided (around 1.4% of cases in the country, depending on the year). This represents average savings between USD 7230 and 82,207 per year, depending on the severity of the impact on individuals with dengue. Our study demonstrates that forest conservation can serve as a public health investment, enhancing social welfare by mitigating illness and reducing associated healthcare expenditures. Our results must be interpreted with caution, however, as the characteristics of our data prevent us from confirming that the estimated negative effect of forest cover on dengue represents a causal impact.
articles.abstract_cn: 大约有3.9亿人面临登革热感染风险，登革热是由蚊子传播的一组病毒（Halstead in Annu Rev Entomol 53:273-291, 2008. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.ento.53.103106.0933262008 ; WHO in WHO | Dengue and severe dengue, Geneva, 2018）。在2019年，中美洲遭受了严重的登革热疫情（Salinas Maldonado in Un brote de dengue pone en alerta a Centroamérica | Sociedad | EL PAÍS, El País, 2019）。哥斯达黎加在2019年的前24个流行病学周内，登革热病例数几乎比去年同期翻了一番（Ávalos in Costa Rica casi duplica número de enfermos de dengue en lo que va del año, con respecto al 2018, La Nación, 2019）。在美洲，森林覆盖被认为减少了蚊子的 anthropogenic 栖息地，同时也增加了其捕食者的存在（Vasilakis et al. in Nat Rev Microbiol 9:532-541, 2011. https://doi.org/10.1038/nrmicro2595 ; Weterings et al. in Basic Appl Ecol 15:486-495, 2014a. https://doi.org/10.1016/J.BAAE.2014.07.006 ）。在本研究中，我们使用计量经济学模型将住院记录与2001和2011年的森林覆盖图联系起来，估计增加森林覆盖对哥斯达黎加登革热患病率的边际效应。我们发现，增加森林覆盖百分比显著减少了登革热住院人数和疫情爆发的概率。使用相同的模型，我们预测如果在10年间森林覆盖率增加三个百分点（每年0.29%），每年可能避免29例登革热住院（约占全国病例的1.4%，取决于年份）。这代表平均每年节省美元7230至82,207，具体取决于登革热患者影响的严重程度。我们的研究表明，森林保护可以作为公共卫生投资，通过减轻疾病和减少相关医疗支出来提高社会福利。然而，我们的结果必须谨慎解读，因为我们的数据特征使我们无法确认森林覆盖对登革热的估计负效应代表因果关系。

articles.title_en: Forest Fires, Smoky Kitchens, and Human Health in Indonesia
articles.title_cn: 森林火灾、烟雾厨房与印度尼西亚的人类健康
articles.abstract_en: Burning tropical forests to establish lucrative agricultural crops ignores potentially important health externalities of the resulting air pollution. These health externalities are often poorly understood, especially if other environmental hazards, such as indoor pollution, are not taken into account. Given the potential for joint, contemporaneous harms, we estimate the impacts of outdoor and indoor air pollution on respiratory health in Indonesia. To address the endogeneity of air pollution exposure, we use panel fixed effects estimation and instrument for outdoor pollution using upwind forest fire intensity. We find that outdoor air pollution exposure reduces lung capacity and decreases overall health status. Subgroup analysis reveals that these impacts are higher among the youngest and oldest individuals in our sample. Critically, we find suggestive evidence that outdoor air pollution exposure is more harmful to the health of individuals living in households that use clean cooking fuels. Thus, policies aimed at reducing environmental health harms are not substitutable—that is, reductions in both indoor and outdoor air pollution exposures are necessary for achieving health targets.
articles.abstract_cn: 焚烧热带森林以建立利润丰厚的农业作物，忽视了由此产生的空气污染可能带来的重要健康外部性。这些健康外部性往往未被充分理解，尤其是在未考虑室内污染等其他环境危害的情况下。鉴于存在联合、同时发生的危害的可能性，我们估计了印度尼西亚室外和室内空气污染对呼吸系统健康的影响。为解决空气污染暴露的内生性问题，我们使用面板固定效应估计，并利用上风向森林火灾强度作为室外污染的工具变量。我们发现，室外空气污染暴露会降低肺活量并降低整体健康状况。亚组分析显示，这些影响在样本中最年轻和最年长的个体中更为显著。重要的是，我们发现有提示性证据表明，室外空气污染暴露对使用清洁烹饪燃料的家庭中的个体健康危害更大。因此，旨在减少环境健康危害的政策不可替代——也就是说，减少室内和室外空气污染暴露对于实现健康目标都是必要的。

articles.title_en: Optimal Ecosystem Change in the Presence of Ecosystem-Mediated Human Health Impacts
articles.title_cn: 存在生态系统介导的人类健康影响时的最优生态系统变化
articles.abstract_en: A growing body of empirical evidence suggests that land use change, and the resulting decline in both the area and quality of natural habitats, contributes to an increased incidence of disease in humans. Despite calls to leverage conservation policy to address the burden of disease linked to ecosystem change, the potential benefits are unknown. Efficiently reducing the burden of infectious disease through land use policies and conservation initiatives is challenging because it requires balancing trade-offs that depend on ecological and socioeconomic factors. To assess some of these trade-offs, we developed a dynamic model of optimal land use when ecosystem change affects the overall incidence of infectious disease. We compared the net benefits and paths of optimal policy in which the increased cost of disease resulting from natural habitat loss is included in the optimization with a base case where it is ignored. We found that ignoring the linkage between habitat degradation and infectious disease incidence in the planner’s problem reduces the net benefits of land management, such as conservation efforts, and results in significantly higher rates of infection and health costs.
articles.abstract_cn: 越来越多的实证证据表明，土地利用变化以及由此导致的自然栖息地面积和质量下降，会增加人类疾病的发病率。尽管有人呼吁利用保护政策来解决与生态系统变化相关的疾病负担，但其潜在益处尚不清楚。通过土地利用政策和保护举措有效减少传染病负担具有挑战性，因为这需要平衡依赖于生态和社会经济因素的权衡。为了评估其中一些权衡，我们开发了一个动态模型，用于在生态系统变化影响传染病总体发病率时确定最优土地利用。我们将自然栖息地丧失导致的疾病成本增加纳入优化，并将其与忽略该成本的基准情况下的最优政策的净收益和路径进行了比较。我们发现，在规划者的问题中忽略栖息地退化与传染病发病率之间的联系，会降低土地管理（如保护努力）的净收益，并导致显著更高的感染率和健康成本。

articles.title_en: Forest Mitigates Short-Term Health Risk of Air Pollution: Evidence from China
articles.title_cn: 森林缓解空气污染短期健康风险：来自中国的证据
articles.abstract_en: This study assembles satellite data, individual-level death records, and air quality data to estimate forest greenness impact on air pollution and health outcomes in China. We find that forest greenness improves air quality. A 10 percentage-points increase in the seasonal average normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) is estimated to increase the overall air quality index (AQI) by 2.6 (3.8% from its mean of 70.8). This NDVI increase predicts decreases in seasonal cardiorespiratory deaths by 1.09% (9.5 people), and in non-cardiorespiratory deaths by 0.87% (7.3 people), ceteris paribus. Also, forest greenness has a mitigating effect of reducing the mortality risk of air pollution as we find that an additional greenness of 10-percentage-point increase in NDVI contributes to a reduction in air pollution-caused mortality by 0.5 people each season. The elderly and especially the elderly males are more likely to benefit from the mitigation by forest greenness possibly because they are more frequently exposed to air pollution and the greenness. A back-of-the-envelope calculation indicates that doubling the greenness of forest would bring about a health benefit that is far beyond an order of magnitude larger than the cost of forest conservation efforts.
articles.abstract_cn: 本研究整合卫星数据、个体层面死亡记录和空气质量数据，以估计中国森林绿化对空气污染和健康结果的影响。我们发现森林绿化改善了空气质量。季节性平均归一化植被指数（NDVI）每增加10个百分点，总体空气质量指数（AQI）估计增加2.6（相对于其均值70.8的3.8%）。在其他条件不变的情况下，这一NDVI增加预测季节性心肺疾病死亡人数减少1.09%（9.5人），非心肺疾病死亡人数减少0.87%（7.3人）。此外，森林绿化具有降低空气污染死亡风险的缓解效应，我们发现NDVI每额外增加10个百分点，每个季节因空气污染导致的死亡人数减少0.5人。老年人，尤其是老年男性，更可能受益于森林绿化的缓解作用，这可能是因为他们更频繁地暴露于空气污染和绿化环境中。一项粗略计算表明，将森林绿化翻倍所带来的健康效益将远超森林保护措施成本的十倍以上。
